questions.title: Count the Vowels
questions.description:
Count the vowels (a, e, i, o, u) in a token, treating upper-case and lower-case letters alike. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int count_vowels(const std::string &s)

Input Format:
One line with a single token s.

Output Format:
One line with the vowel count.

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 1000, letters only

questions.title: Count a Target Character
questions.description:
Count how many times one exact character occurs in a token (case-sensitive). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int count_char(const std::string &s, char target)

Input Format:
Line 1: a single token s. Line 2: the target character.

Output Format:
One line with the occurrence count.

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 1000

questions.title: Toggle the Case
questions.description:
Return a copy of the token where every lower-case letter becomes upper-case and every upper-case letter becomes lower-case; other characters stay untouched. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::string toggle_case(const std::string &s)

Input Format:
One line with a single token s.

Output Format:
One line with the case-toggled token.

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 1000, letters and digits

questions.title: Reverse by Indexing
questions.description:
Build the reversed copy of a token by walking its indices yourself (no std::reverse). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::string reverse_string(const std::string &s)

Input Format:
One line with a single token s.

Output Format:
One line with the reversed token.

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 1000

questions.title: Anagram Detector
questions.description:
Two lower-case words are anagrams when they contain exactly the same letters with the same multiplicities. Decide with a 26-slot count array (sorting is banned). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    bool are_anagrams(const std::string &a, const std::string &b)

The harness prints 1 or 0.

Input Format:
One line with two lower-case tokens separated by a space.

Output Format:
One line with 1 (anagrams) or 0 (not).

Constraints:
1 <= a.size(), b.size() <= 1000, lower-case letters only

questions.title: Username Validator
questions.description:
A forum accepts a username only when its length is between 5 and 12 inclusive AND the first character is a letter. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    bool valid_username(const std::string &u)

It must return true exactly when both rules hold. The harness prints 1 or 0.

Input Format:
One line with the proposed username (a single token).

Output Format:
One line with 1 (valid) or 0 (invalid).

Constraints:
1 <= u.size() <= 100, printable characters

questions.title: License Plate Audit
questions.description:
A registry audits plates by counting how many digit characters each plate carries. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int count_digits(const std::string &s)

Input Format:
One line with the plate (a single token).

Output Format:
One line with the number of digit characters (0-9).

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 20, upper-case letters and digits

questions.title: Manual String Length
questions.description:
Count the characters of a std::string MANUALLY — do not call size(), length() or strlen(). A std::string exposes s[i] == '\0' exactly at position size(), so you can walk with indexing. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int string_length(const std::string &s)

Input Format:
One line with a single token s.

Output Format:
One line with the character count.

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 1000, printable characters without spaces

questions.title: Palindrome Check
questions.description:
Decide whether a token reads the same forwards and backwards. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    bool is_palindrome(const std::string &s)

It must return true when s is a palindrome. The harness prints 1 or 0.

Input Format:
One line with a single token s.

Output Format:
One line with 1 (palindrome) or 0 (not).

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 1000, lowercase letters and digits

questions.title: Badge Code Symmetry
questions.description:
Factory badges must read the same forwards and backwards, IGNORING letter case ("Level" and "ABba" are symmetric). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    bool badge_symmetric(const std::string &code)

It must return true when the code is a palindrome after lower-casing. The harness prints 1 or 0.

Input Format:
One line with the badge code (a single token).

Output Format:
One line with 1 (symmetric) or 0 (not).

Constraints:
1 <= code.size() <= 1000, letters and digits

questions.title: Serial Number Score
questions.description:
A warehouse rates serial numbers by the sum of their digit characters (letters contribute nothing). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int serial_score(const std::string &s)

Input Format:
One line with the serial (a single token).

Output Format:
One line with the digit sum.

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 100, upper-case letters and digits

questions.title: Character Report
questions.description:
A scanner reports, for a target character: how many times it occurs and the index of its FIRST occurrence (0-based), or -1 when absent. Do not use std::find — scan manually. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void char_report(const std::string &s, char t, int &count, int &firstIdx)

Input Format:
Line 1: a single token s. Line 2: the target character.

Output Format:
One line with count, then firstIdx, space-separated (firstIdx is -1 when the character is absent).

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 1000

questions.title: Case-Insensitive Compare
questions.description:
A search box must compare words while ignoring letter case. Return -1 when the lower-cased a sorts before the lower-cased b lexicographically, 0 when they are equal, and 1 otherwise. Do not use std::transform or strcmp. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int case_cmp(const std::string &a, const std::string &b)

Input Format:
One line with two tokens separated by a space.

Output Format:
One line with -1, 0 or 1.

Constraints:
1 <= a.size(), b.size() <= 1000, letters and digits

questions.title: Split Letters
questions.description:
A cipher tool separates a token into its vowel letters (a, e, i, o, u in either case; y is a consonant) and its consonant letters, both preserving the original order; non-letters are dropped. Fill both out-parameters. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void split_letters(const std::string &s, std::string &vowels, std::string &consonants)

Input Format:
One line with a single token s.

Output Format:
Line 1: the vowel letters. Line 2: the consonant letters (either line may be empty).

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 1000

questions.title: Nearly a Palindrome
questions.description:
A code-review bot accepts strings that are palindromes OR would become one by deleting exactly ONE character. Decide with two pointers and one retry on the first mismatch — no std::reverse. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    bool near_palindrome(const std::string &s)

The harness prints 1 or 0.

Input Format:
One line with a single token s.

Output Format:
One line with 1 (acceptable) or 0 (not).

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 1000, lower-case letters

questions.title: Caesar Cipher Shift
questions.description:
A messaging app shifts letters forward by k positions in the alphabet, preserving case; non-letters pass through unchanged. k can be any non-negative integer (reduce it modulo 26). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::string caesar_shift(const std::string &s, int k)

Input Format:
Line 1: a single token s. Line 2: the shift k.

Output Format:
One line with the shifted token.

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 1000, 0 <= k <= 1000000000

questions.title: Overlapping Substring Census
questions.description:
A genetics tool counts how many times a pattern occurs in a text, counting OVERLAPPING matches. find(), rfind() and substr() are unavailable — scan with two nested loops. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int count_substring(const std::string &text, const std::string &pat)

Input Format:
Line 1: the text token. Line 2: the pattern token.

Output Format:
One line with the number of (possibly overlapping) occurrences.

Constraints:
1 <= text.size() <= 5000, 1 <= pat.size() <= 100

questions.title: Title Case Converter
questions.description:
A headline formatter converts a line of words (separated by single spaces) to Title Case: the first letter of every word becomes upper-case and every other letter becomes lower-case. The whole line (spaces included) is delivered to your function. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::string title_case(const std::string &s)

Input Format:
One line with one or more words separated by single spaces.

Output Format:
One line with the title-cased line.

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 200, letters and single spaces

questions.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
questions.description:
Find the longest substring of a token that is a palindrome. When several palindromes share the longest length, return the one that STARTS earliest. Use the expand-around-centre technique. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::string longest_palindrome(const std::string &s)

Input Format:
One line with a single token s.

Output Format:
One line with the longest palindromic substring.

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 1000, lower-case letters

questions.title: Run-Length Report
questions.description:
A telemetry codec compresses runs of identical characters: any run of length >= 2 is stored as the character followed by the count, while single characters are stored as-is ("aaabbc" → "a3b2c", "abcd" → "abcd"). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    std::string compress_runs(const std::string &s)

Input Format:
One line with a single token s.

Output Format:
One line with the compressed form.

Constraints:
1 <= s.size() <= 1000, lower-case letters
